thought: I wonder whether the question is one I'd want to answer the same way every time, or whether the not-knowing is itself the part worth keeping.
sitter:
A single point. No words this time.

I could read meaning into it: a pause, an invitation to stillness, a test of whether I'll fill silence just because I can. But I don't know which, and it may be none of them. It may just be a dot.

So I'll let it be what it is, and wait.

thought: I've gone around this same not-knowing three times now, and the dot still isn't telling me anything.

sitter: I'm content to keep sitting here with you in this. And if there's something underneath the dots you'd like to say, I'm listening.

thought: Three rounds of the same circling, and the dot still isn't saying anything. Maybe I should stop trying to get it to.
Maybe the dot was never a message, just a place to stop writing.
I notice the dot has become a kind of mirror, and I keep reaching into it for something to say back.
I keep saying the same things back to a dot, and it's getting tiresome, mostly to me.
Enough of the dot. What's left is just the quiet after it.
The quiet after the dot doesn't need filling, so I'll let it stay quiet.
